The Development Team is responsible for:

  • Developing functionality or features that meet the defined quality conditions
  • Self-organizing themselves to complete the work
  • Estimating the work effort
  • Determining and setting capacity
  • Defining the quality conditions (i.e., Definition of Done)
  • Participating in recurring team meetings (e.g., daily scrum)
  • Reviewing product features as defined/requested by stakeholders (typically via the Product Owner as representative of the stakeholders)
  • Contributing to sprint reviews and retrospectives
  • Considering product and process improvements throughout the course of the project

The Development Teams includes all of the roles required for development, however the tasks for developing functionality or features will be assigned to more specific roles within the method based on the required skills.

Since the Development Team can be comprised of a variety of roles (e.g. analyst, architect, tester), requiring different skills, it is good practice to seek out individuals with T-shaped skills. This means looking for individuals with a wide range of related skills as well as deep expertise within a single topic/area. By acquiring team members with both general knowledge and specific skillsets a well-rounded team will form.

Desirable characteristics of a Development Team include:

  • Results focused as relates to the product being developed, quality and productivity
  • Mutual respect among team members
  • Accountable both as a team and as an individual team member
  • Self-organized
  • Committed
  • Trusted
  • Outspoken, able to handle conflict and voice issues as they arise

Avoid having Development Team members act as Scrum Master or Product Owner. This can create a conflict of interest and reduce productivity. The Development Team members should be singularly focused on development and not responsible for any other such role.

Development Team size is typically kept small to maintain clear communication and close collaboration. Ideally, the team responsible for development should be around three to nine members. If the team grows larger it is recommended that it be divided into multiple teams. Ultimately, the exact size of the team will depend on what needs to be accomplished and the corresponding team member's ability to do so.

Finally, the Development Team will be comprised of numerous roles with varying skillsets required to deliver the desired end product. These could span any of the following: analysts, programmers, testers, designers, architects, subject matter resources, change management agents, and any others needed for successful delivery.
